entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv15563"/><div sID="gen29995" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv15563"/><hi type="bold">22-28. a man approved of God--</hi>rather, "authenticated," "proved," or "demonstrated to be from God."<div eID="gen29995" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29996" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">by miracles ... which God did by him--</hi>This is not a low view of our Lord's miracles, as has been alleged, nor inconsistent with <reference osisRef="John.2.11">Joh 2:11</reference>, but is in strict accordance with His progress from humiliation to glory, and with His own words in <reference osisRef="John.5.19">Joh 5:19</reference>. This view of Christ is here dwelt on to exhibit to the Jews the whole course of Jesus of Nazareth as the ordinance and doing of the God of Israel [Alford]. <div eID="gen29996" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv15568"/><div sID="gen30004" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv15568"/><hi type="bold">29-36. David ... is ... dead and buried, &c.--</hi>Peter, full of the Holy Ghost, sees in this sixteenth Psalm, one Holy Man, whose life of high devotedness and lofty spirituality is crowned with the assurance, that though He taste of death, He shall rise again without seeing corruption, and be admitted to the bliss of God's immediate presence. Now as this was palpably untrue of David, it could be meant only of One other, even of Him whom David was taught to expect as the final Occupant of the throne of Israel. (Those, therefore, and they are many, who take David himself to be the subject of this Psalm, and the words quoted to refer to Christ only in a more eminent sense, nullify the whole argument of the apostle). The Psalm is then affirmed to have had its only proper fulfilment in Jesus, of whose resurrection and ascension they were witnesses, while the glorious effusion of the Spirit by the hand of the ascended One, setting an infallible seal upon all, was even then witnessed by the thousands who stood listening to Him. A further illustration of Messiah's ascension and session at God's right hand is drawn from <reference osisRef="Ps.110.1">Psa 110:1</reference>, in which David cannot be thought to speak of himself, seeing he is still in his grave. <div eID="gen30004" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv15570"/><div sID="gen30010" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv15570"/><hi type="bold">37-40. pricked in their hearts--</hi>the begun fulfilment of <reference osisRef="Zech.12.10">Zec 12:10</reference>, whose full accomplishment is reserved for the day when "all Israel shall be saved" (see on <reference osisRef="Rom.11.26">Ro 11:26</reference>).<div eID="gen30010" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30011" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">what shall we do?--</hi>This is that beautiful spirit of genuine compunction and childlike docility, which, discovering its whole past career to have been one frightful mistake, seeks only to be set right for the future, be the change involved and the sacrifices required what they may. So Saul of Tarsus (<reference osisRef="Acts.9.6">Ac 9:6</reference>). <div eID="gen30011" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv15574"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Acts.2.41-Acts.2.47">Ac 2:41-47</reference>. Beautiful Beginnings of the Christian Church.</title> <div sID="gen30018" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv15574"/><hi type="bold">41-47. they that gladly received his word were baptized--</hi>"It is difficult to say how three thousand could be baptized in one day, according to the old practice of a complete submersion; and the more as in Jerusalem there was no water at hand except Kidron and a few pools. The difficulty can only be removed by supposing that they already employed sprinkling, or baptized in houses in large vessels. Formal submersion in rivers, or larger quantities of water, probably took place only where the locality conveniently allowed it" [Olshausen].<div eID="gen30018" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30019" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the same day there were added to them about three thousand souls--</hi>fitting inauguration of the new kingdom, as an economy of the Spirit! <div eID="gen30019" type="x-p"/>

The difficulty can only be removed by supposing that they already employed sprinkling, or baptized in houses in large vessels. Formal submersion in rivers, or larger quantities of water, probably took place only where the locality conveniently allowed it" [Olshausen]. the same day there were added to them about three thousand souls-- fitting inauguration of the new kingdom, as an economy of the Spirit!
